chunks.arabic_text: وَسَأَلَ عُمَرُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ:

translations.en: ʿUmar ibn Yazīd asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

chunks.arabic_text: عَنْ إِمَامٍ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ فِي جَمِيعِ أُمُورِهِ عَارِفٍ غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ يُسْمِعُ أَبَوَيْهِ الْكَلَامَ الْغَلِيظَ الَّذِي يَغِيظُهُمَا أَقْرَأُ خَلْفَهُ

translations.en: About an Imam with whom there is no fault in all his affairs, knowledgeable, except that he makes his parents hear harsh speech that angers them: should I recite behind him?

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ «لَا، تَقْرَأُ خَلْفَهُ مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ عَاقًّا قَاطِعًا.

translations.en: He said: “No, recite behind him so long as he is not disobedient and severing ties.”

en.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of praying behind an Imam whose general conduct and knowledge are sound, but who speaks harshly to his parents. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام indicates that such behavior is blameworthy, yet the prayer behind him is not rejected unless he reaches the level of being openly undutiful and cutting off kinship ties.
en.seo_question: Can one pray behind an Imam who speaks harshly to his parents?

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader being asked about
key_terms.تَقْرَأُ خَلْفَهُ: recite behind him in congregational prayer
